content: When there is no peace in the family, filial piety begins. When the country falls into chaos, patriotism appears.
author: Lao Tzu
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Lao Tzu understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
